nodes.label: kc-21psi-no-margin
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED Avoid 21 psi maps on local fuel entirely
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Refuted for normal conditions. On this map pulls hold the floor in cool air; margin shrinks in hot traffic, and that is what the app watches. Higher untested maps stay untested. See the current card.

nodes.label: kc-after-flash
nodes.description: The after-flash pattern is reassurance, not an alarm
nodes.applies_when: A Drive starts with a Fuel-quality score above the Baseline after a Flash.
nodes.body: After every new Flash KTuner sets the Fuel-quality score to 0.59, and it falls back to the Baseline with calm driving. A start at or below 0.60 that settles toward 0.49 is what a fresh flash does. It is never an Unexplained change, and it never sets a Verdict on its own. Give it ten to fifteen calm minutes before judging fuel or heat, because the score needs that long to relearn. If the score does not settle, or if it climbs again in traffic, that later rise is the finding, judged on its own. The Shakedown drive exists for exactly this pattern.

nodes.label: kc-boost-by-gear
nodes.description: Boost By Gear Limits only limit, and yours are off
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks about Boost By Gear, or how KTuner protects a CVT.
nodes.body: Boost By Gear Limits is one table per gear, rpm by atmospheric pressure, and it only limits: wherever the boost table asks less, the table wins, so values above every target mean no limit. Your map holds 35.4 psi everywhere, so no gear limit is active. KTuner's own tool for sparing a CVT is a first-gear limit, and its quick settings offer flat or ramped versions. The app explains it and does not write this table, and which gear number your CVT reports to it is unconfirmed.

nodes.label: kc-boost-codes
nodes.description: Boost codes P0046 and P0299, and what to log
nodes.applies_when: The owner reports P0046 or P0299, a limp with a dead pedal, or boost that misses target.
nodes.body: P0046 means the ECU can't hold the wastegate where it commands it. On this generation owners traced it to a sticking wastegate actuator, and to a pinhole leak in the vacuum line on the charge pipe; a new downpipe seemed to fix it only for a while. P0299 is underboost. In your log, compare EWG Position with EWG Target, and boost with its target: a position that doesn't follow its target points to the actuator; boost under target with the wastegate shut points to a leak or the turbo's limit. Fix the hardware first; no map change.

nodes.label: kc-boost-step
nodes.description: More boost, one proven step at a time
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks for more boost, or asks how a boost raise would be proven.
nodes.body: A Boost step adds 1 psi to Boost Target 2 Normal, Low and High cam, 3,500 to 4,500 rpm rows, never above the Final Boost Target peak, 23.4 here. Only the second tune gets it; a proven step is copied to the others. Offered when the latest Cool drive holds two floored pulls held 4 seconds above 3,500 rpm and a hot drive passes too. Floored is pedal 85 percent or more until a key-on reading sets it: on these cars floored reads 100 to 113, yours never above 94. Gates: target moved; under- and overshoot held half a second within 1.5 psi, total at most 24; timing within 1 degree of the last proven version; Knock Control settled, at most 0.56 below 5,200 rpm; mixture never leaner than 12.0; fuel pressure at least 90 percent of target. The first failure undoes it.

nodes.label: kc-cvt
nodes.description: CVT care is heat management, not a torque number
nodes.applies_when: Any reply that judges CVT fluid temperature, slip, or hard driving in heat.
nodes.body: The old keep-torque-under-a-number warning is removed: the app sets no torque number for this car, but the ECU's own factory torque limiter still protects the CVT and can pull boost back. What the logs can judge is fluid heat and slip. Watch starts at 90 °C of fluid temperature, and Stop at 100 °C is provisional, not yet seen on this car, whose peak is 95 °C. No pulls with the fluid at or above 90 °C, and never brake-launch: failures owners report come from launching and heavy low-end torque, not from steady pulls. Slip shows as revs jumping without speed, with zero such events across all drives here. The fluid is the Honda HCF-2 grade, changed on the severe schedule on a tuned car in hot traffic.

nodes.label: kc-downpipe
nodes.description: What a downpipe changes on this car, and what it doesn't
nodes.applies_when: The owner has fitted or plans a downpipe, or asks what the map should change for it.
nodes.body: A downpipe lowers the back pressure after the turbo, so the same boost arrives a little sooner; on Civic X dynos torque came 200 to 400 rpm earlier. The parts vendor claims +7 to +12 whp with no tune; no independent dyno exists for this car. Your logs were all recorded with the downpipe and front pipe fitted, so that gain is already in them. No Honda tuner changes the map for a downpipe on the stock turbo, and nothing changes on fuel or spark: the full-load target stays 11.0 and timing is untouched. The one possible map action is a small boost trim, and only if a log proves boost holds above target. After fitting, check both flanges for leaks with the engine cold: a leak shows on the rear oxygen sensor and the catalyst code, not on the front A/F sensor.

nodes.label: kc-downpipe-catted-catless
nodes.description: Catted or catless downpipe: which one, and what each costs
nodes.topics: downpipe, catless, catted, cel, inspection, exhaust
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks which downpipe to buy, or whether a catless pipe is worth it.
nodes.body: The 400-cell catted pipes from TSP and RV6 claim no warning light, and most owners report none, though a few see the rear-sensor code P2A01, or a light only in heavy rain or on long highway runs: that is still the shop's pick. The 200-cell 27WON pipe sets P0420 for most owners within days. Catless makes about 0 to 6 whp over a good catted pipe (owner and vendor reports), brings exhaust smell into the cabin, always sets P0420, and risks the đăng kiểm tailpipe gas test; an unapproved modification can also be fined 65 to 75 million VND. The tune response is the same for all three: no map change, and a small boost trim only if a log proves boost holds above target. Ask which pipe is fitted: older RV6 pipes were 300-cell.

nodes.label: kc-drive-brief
nodes.description: The Baseline drive brief, step by step
nodes.applies_when: Before the first log, after a Flash or Install, or whenever the owner asks how to log a drive the app can read.
nodes.body: Log it like a shop asks. Before you drive: in TunerView turn on every gauge the app reads (AFR Command and MAF Hz included) and set the fastest rate it offers, 10 Hz or more. Go before 8 am or after an hour parked in shade, so the intake is under 42 °C. Drive 10 minutes normally until coolant is above 80 °C. Cruise steady at several speeds for trims. Then, on a straight, empty, legal road, in S: from a 50 km/h roll press the pedal fully and hold it to 100 km/h, then lift. Cruise a minute to cool and do the second pull, starting with intake under 48 °C. Keep at least 10 minutes of moving time in the log, then export the CSV.

nodes.label: kc-dual-boost-targets
nodes.description: How KTuner picks between the dual boost targets
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks what the ECO button does to boost, or which boost table is in use.
nodes.body: Dual Boost Targets With ECO Button gives each tune two boost tables: on the 1.5T the ECU uses Boost Target ECO while the ECO button is on and Boost Target Normal otherwise, so Sport runs the Normal table too. On Starter 21 Dual Tune 2 that is 18 psi in ECO and 21 psi in Normal. The button is the switch: no flash, no device. Use ECO on hot days, in traffic, or on fuel you don't trust. No log channel records ECO, so note it when you attach a log and compare only drives in the same mode.

nodes.label: kc-e10
nodes.description: E10 needs no extra fuel and no trim offset
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks about E10, fuel quality, or adding fuel for ethanol.
nodes.body: Pure gasoline burns at 14.7 and ethanol at 9.0, so E10 lands at 14.1 and needs about 4.3 percent more fuel by mass for the same lambda. The ECU delivers that itself: the front sensor and the trims in closed loop, the fuel model in open loop. E10 carries about 3.4 percent less energy per litre, so economy drops a little and nothing else changes. Vietnam RON95 is about US 90 by Honda's own octane scale and 90 to 91 by the usual estimate: at or just under the 91 that KTuner asks for. Cruise trims sit near 0.8 percent negative on E10, so no E10 offset is ever written into the airflow curve, and WOT stays judged against the map's own target.

nodes.label: kc-e10-trim-baseline
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED Expect a few percent positive trim on E10
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Refuted by data. Cruise trims on E10 sit near zero, not a few percent positive, so no E10 baseline is ever subtracted before judging trims or correcting airflow. See the current card for the measured values.

nodes.label: kc-expectations
nodes.description: The turbo has no headroom left on this map
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks for more boost or more power, or a reply explains a flat pull.
nodes.body: The Starter 21 map asks 18 psi in ECO and 21 psi in Normal and Sport, and the file tops out at 23.4 psi of final target. These logs were measured with a downpipe and front pipe already fitted: at the highest boost logged, up to 19.9 psi, the wastegate sits about 2.5 percent open, against 8.0 percent at idle and cruise and 65.5 percent at its most open. Nearly all exhaust already drives the turbine, so more boost mostly means more heat, not more power. KTuner claims the map adds up to 58 lb-ft, or 79 Nm, over a stock car rated 240 Nm and 176 hp. Gains from here come from cooler air and good habits, and more boost only from a step proven on your logs. Most drives end with no map change, and that is an answer, not a gap.

nodes.label: kc-final-boost-target
nodes.description: Final Boost Target passes the target through and caps it
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks what Final Boost Target does, or whether it limits boost.
nodes.body: Final Boost Target takes the incoming target, from the boost table, the part-pedal target or the Boost By Gear limit, passes it nearly one to one, and caps it at its last column header. Raising that cap means changing the header and its whole column. On your map every column is the same in every rpm row and the top is 23.4 psi, so it passes your target through and is not what holds a pull below the table. The app explains it and never edits it.

nodes.label: kc-flash-howto
nodes.description: Flashing with KTuner: power, the key, and what is normal after
nodes.applies_when: The owner is about to flash, a flash failed, or warning lights came on after a flash.
nodes.body: Put a battery charger on the car and power the V2 from a strong port: low voltage is what fails flashes. Ignition on, engine off, never running. When it finishes, key off for ten seconds, back on, and wait for flash successful. Warning lights during the flash are normal, and driver-assist warnings can stay until you have driven ten to fifteen minutes. A failed flash leaves the car unable to start: reconnect and accept recovery, which returns it to factory. A Recovery prompt while the engine runs means a loose cable: say no. Error codes right after a flash usually mean the wrong codebase: start the tune with the one that matches the unit info. If the V2 stops waking with the car, set CAN Gateway to Yes. Saving a tune to the V2 is not flashing it: the next log proves the change.

nodes.label: kc-fuel-test
nodes.description: Is premium fuel worth it? Test it tank against tank
nodes.topics: fuel, ron97, ron95, e10, premium, knock, experiment
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks whether E10 RON97 III is worth it, or logs a drive on a different fuel.
nodes.body: Better fuel is judged by Knock Control, tank against tank, never by feel. Petrolimex sells no RON97; smaller retailers sell E10 RON97 III. On cool drives both fuels sit at the 0.49 floor, so only a hot pair can show a difference. Drive your usual E10 RON95 III until Knock Control settles, then log a hot drive. Run the tank low, fill E10 RON97 III, drive calmly until it settles again, and log the same hot drive: same route, same mode, same map slot, intake within 8 °C. Tag each log with its fuel. Read Knock Control and timing at or below 5,200 rpm only, because above that the ECU raises the score on purpose. A gap of 0.5 degrees or less is inside KTuner's logging step: no measurable gain. The most RON97 can win back is what heat costs, about 1.6 degrees.

nodes.label: kc-heat-soak
nodes.description: Heat soak, not the tune, costs this car performance
nodes.applies_when: A Drive runs hot, pulls start with hot intake air, or boost falls on a hot afternoon.
nodes.body: Every drive started soon after another one begins with 57 to 64 °C in the manifold. Cool drives read 35 to 39 °C while moving, and a pull should start at or below 48 °C. The intercooler is not the problem: under boost it adds only 2 to 6 °C over the inlet air. Two drives half an hour apart prove it: pull-start intake 49 °C against 60 °C, peak boost 19.9 psi against 16.7 psi, and the timed run 1.77 s against 2.23 s. After a hot stop, drive three to five calm minutes before any hard acceleration, and judge power only between drives at similar intake temperatures.

nodes.label: kc-high-rpm
nodes.description: Score rises above 5,200 rpm do not count while the artificial rise is on
nodes.applies_when: A Drive shows Fuel-quality score rises at high revs.
nodes.body: Non-Si ECUs raise Knock Control on purpose above about 5,200 rpm. KTuner can remove it with Quick Enables, Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise; on this car's Starter map that box is off, so the rise is present, and the Car profile records the box. While it is off, those rises say nothing about fuel quality or heat and are excluded from fuel and heat verdicts; the forced rise costs about 2 degrees only at the top of a pull. If the box is ever ticked, a rise up there is real knock and counts like any other. This owner rarely revs past 5,200 rpm. Judge the tank by what the score does in normal driving and in traffic, where heat and lugging are the real movers.

nodes.label: kc-iat-retard
nodes.description: Why hot intake air costs power: IAT Ignition
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks why the car feels slower when hot, or what intake temperature does to timing.
nodes.body: Hot intake air costs timing on a schedule, before any knock. This map's IAT Ignition High Load (Retard) takes nothing up to 40 °C, 4.5 degrees at 50 °C and 9 degrees at 90 °C and above; at low load it takes 1 to 3 degrees. KTuner applies it through the knock limit, so it can take up to that much as the air heats, and on E10 RON95 Knock Control rises in heat and pulls more on top. That is why a heat-soaked pull makes less power on the same map, and why the cure is cooler intake air and a few calm minutes after a hot stop, not a map change.

nodes.label: kc-iat2-side
nodes.description: IAT is after the intercooler, IAT2 before the turbo
nodes.topics: heat, iat, iat2, intercooler, sensors, gauges
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks what IAT2 measures, or a reply would judge the intercooler from IAT2.
nodes.body: On this car IAT is the manifold air after the intercooler and IAT2 the inlet air before the turbo. Under boost IAT reads 2 to 6 °C above IAT2, which only works that way round, and KTuner's gauge names and owners of the same engine label them the same. So the intercooler is judged by IAT minus IAT2 under boost: a gap that grows over back-to-back pulls means it is saturating. Some owners report other ECUs of this engine the other way round, so on a new car check the sign of the gap before trusting it.

nodes.label: kc-ignition-formula
nodes.description: How the ECU sets final ignition, with KTuner's own example
nodes.topics: ignition, retard, formula, tables, ktuner, datalog
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks how timing is decided, why Actual Ign is lower than the table, or what Knock Retard means.
nodes.body: KTuner's help gives the rule: ignition table plus knock ignition limitation, minus knock retard, is the final timing, and the ECU uses the lesser of that and the table, so it never runs more than the table. Knock retard is Knock Control times the knock retard table. Their example: 21 plus 2 is 23 degrees; Knock Control 0.38 times a table value of 10 is 3.8 degrees of retard, so the final is 19.2. The log shows both in steps and cuts down rather than rounding: the example logs the retard as 3.5. On TunerView, ignition and retard both move in half-degree steps; the one-degree ignition step is for OBD loggers. Under boost every score from 0.49 to 0.54 logs the same 5 degrees of retard, so read Knock Control itself. Follow Actual Ign, Knock Control and Knock Retard together, and never read meaning into a half-degree change.

nodes.label: kc-knock-070
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED No hard driving from 0.70
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Replaced. The forum figure sat above where this car already loses timing everywhere, so no-hard-driving starts lower, held over a full minute. See the current card for the timing-cost cut points.

nodes.label: kc-log-channels
nodes.description: The gauges the shop reads, by their KTuner names
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks which gauges to log, what a gauge abbreviation means, or why a log reads Can't tell.
nodes.body: KTuner's short gauge names and the CSV's long names are the same gauges. K.Cont is Knock Control, the Fuel-quality score; K.Ret is Knock Retard; A.Ignition is Ignition. TC.Target and TC.Press are Turbo Pressure Target and Turbo Pressure, read at the turbo before the throttle, while MAP is the manifold. EWG.Posi and EWG.Target are the wastegate; DIFPress and DIFP.Target are fuel pressure; Wideband is the O2 column. TPS is your foot on the pedal and TPS.C is TPS Command, the throttle plate. Log bank one trims only: a trim pinned at its lowest value is a wrong bank or a dead channel and reads Can't tell. Your logger already records all of these; still missing are AFR Command and MAF Hz, which the airflow and mixture checks need. Knock Count is a misfire count, not knock.

nodes.label: kc-log-gate
nodes.description: Is the log good enough to read?
nodes.applies_when: Every upload, before any verdict; when a log settles nothing.
nodes.body: A tuner checks the log before the car. Four things make a log readable: a fast enough rate (10 samples a second or more), at least 10 minutes of moving time, no gauge stuck on one number while the revs move, and AFR Command and MAF Hz in the gauge list. Without AFR Command the mixture can only be judged against the map's target, not what the ECU actually asked for; without MAF Hz the airflow sensor's headroom can't be checked. A log that misses the gate is not a failure of the car: fix the logger and drive the brief again.

nodes.label: kc-maf-data-rules
nodes.description: What a log needs before the airflow curve can be corrected
nodes.topics: maf, afm, airflow, trims, calibration, log, drive
nodes.applies_when: Before any MAF Scaling change, or the owner asks how much driving a MAF correction needs.
nodes.body: A MAF correction is only as good as the samples behind each point. The method MAF tools use: an engine fully warm, intake temperature steady, throttle smooth, and the rows around sudden throttle changes, stops and loop transitions thrown away. Each point is corrected from the trims logged at that airflow, averaged so one odd moment can't move it, and a point with too few samples is left alone. The usual guide is at least 30 min of steady cruising, as much mixed driving, and 15 min of slow driving across rounds. Smooth the result once, lightly. Fix part throttle first, then full throttle. Expect two or three rounds: nobody nails it in one shot.

nodes.label: kc-maf-housing
nodes.description: MAF Scaling follows the housing, never the brand
nodes.applies_when: An intake is fitted, trims sit far off after a Flash, or the owner asks which MAF preset to pick.
nodes.body: Ask which housing is fitted before touching anything: factory airbox, a street housing, or a larger Race housing. The street housings read near stock, so they keep the Factory curve. The Race curves read 1.29 to 1.43 times the air at the same sensor frequency, so a Race preset on a street housing runs about forty percent rich and the trims clamp trying to pull it back. After any airflow Flash, drive calm first and make no pull until trims sit within 5 percent. Trims beyond 10 percent across most of the range mean the curve is wrong for the hardware: revert, do not tune around it. Never infer the housing from the brand.

nodes.label: kc-maf-trim-direction
nodes.description: Which way a trim moves the airflow curve
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks how to correct MAF Scaling from a CSV, or which way a trim points.
nodes.body: A positive trim means the ECU added fuel because it measured too little air, so the airflow points covering that airflow move up by about that percent; a negative trim moves them down. Average the trims at each point over warm, steady driving, and throw away the rows where you lift off or coast, which read zero or spike, and the first seconds after a throttle change. Reach the higher points with a slow, steady roll-on, not a stab. Apply part of the correction, keep the curve rising, flash, and log again. On this car only rows below about 8 psi count: above that the trims freeze. Owners and KTuner staff describe the same method.

nodes.label: kc-maf-wot-calibration
nodes.description: How tuners correct the full-throttle end of the airflow curve
nodes.topics: maf, afm, airflow, mixture, wot, calibration, tables, ktuner
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks how to correct MAF from a CSV, or full-throttle mixture is far from AFR Command.
nodes.body: At full throttle the airflow table is corrected against AFR Command, not against trims. Log several full-throttle pulls in the same gear mode at the same intake temperature, with AFR Command and MAF Hz logged. Where the measured mixture is leaner than commanded, the points covering that airflow read too little air; where it is richer, too much. Change only those points, by about 2 % per round, keep the curve smooth, flash, and log the same pulls again. Stop when the mixture sits a little richer than commanded, about 0.2 AFR. Richer than 10.5 means the points are too high. One owner's numbers are never copied to another car, and a blind fixed cut to the top of the curve is not a calibration. Done wrong, this leans the engine at full load, so the shop checks every point before you flash.

nodes.label: kc-map-switching
nodes.description: How KTuner on-the-fly map switching works
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks about map slots, Tune 1, 2 or 3, or switching maps while driving.
nodes.body: On The Fly Map Switching holds three tunes in one map. They differ only in boost targets and Turbo Responsiveness; ignition, fuel, knock and the throttle setting are shared by all three, so a tune cannot carry a fuel's timing. Switch with a long press of the cruise Cancel button; switching while moving is supported. With the KTuner device unplugged the car starts in Tune 1, so Tune 1 holds the proven map and a trial goes in Tune 2. As digitized, the three tunes on this map hold the same boost targets, so switching changes nothing yet. No log channel records the tune: tag each log with its map slot and switch only between logs.

nodes.label: kc-misfire-gauges
nodes.description: The Misfire and count gauges are not the ones to judge by
nodes.applies_when: The owner worries about a Knock Count or Misfire number in TunerView, or asks which gauge matters.
nodes.body: On the 1.5T, the Knock Count and Misfire gauges are not the ones to judge by. KTuner support told owners that the count is tied to misfire detection, and experienced owners ignore both on this platform. The number that matters is the Fuel-quality score: it is the ECU's learned margin, and it is what the shop reads. AFR Adj is not the mixture to watch either: watch the measured AFR against AFR Command. So a rising count on its own is no reason to buy spark plugs or change the map; a step up in the Fuel-quality score is.

nodes.label: kc-octane-booster
nodes.description: Don't add octane booster
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks about octane booster or additives.
nodes.body: Don't add octane booster. KTuner staff, a vendor and the long-running owner reliability thread all advise against it, and one engine failure in the largest owner census lists booster as a possible cause. If you suspect the fuel, try a different busy station, or E10 RON97, and compare tank against tank by Knock Control on matched drives.

nodes.label: kc-oil
nodes.description: Oil grade and keeping the revs up
nodes.applies_when: A Drive shows lugging, or the owner asks about oil for a tuned car.
nodes.body: Use the Honda manual grade 0W-20, rated API SP or newer: those ratings pass an engine test that averages five or fewer early-ignition events per run and never more than eight, while plain older grades require no such test. Lugging means 900 to 1,700 rpm with the foot down, and 31 of all 41 score rises on this car happened there, so the case against it is data, not theory. Below 60 km/h in traffic, use S or a paddle before pressing past a third of the pedal, and let it rev to 2000 rpm or more first. Its top end touches the 1,500 to 2,500 rpm low-speed early-ignition band, which is a second reason to stay out of it.

nodes.label: kc-open-loop-wot
nodes.description: Under boost the trims stop correcting the mixture
nodes.topics: mixture, trims, open-loop, closed-loop, maf, afm, wot, fuel
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks why trims look fine but full-throttle mixture is off, or what open loop means.
nodes.body: On this car it is confirmed from the logs: short-term trim reads exactly zero on every warm row at 12 psi and above, and on nearly all from about 8 psi, while lower down it moves as normal. So under boost the ECU runs open loop: the trims neither correct the mixture nor say anything about the airflow curve there, and only the airflow calibration (MAF Scaling) and the map's target decide it. An airflow correction uses only rows below about 8 psi, where the trims are live. Judge full-throttle mixture against AFR Command, the value the ECU actually asked for, which can differ from the table. Read the loop state from the trims, never from a status number alone.

nodes.label: kc-p0420
nodes.description: P0420 after a downpipe, and the inspection risk
nodes.applies_when: A downpipe is fitted, P0420 appears, or the owner asks about switching the code off.
nodes.body: A downpipe carries the rear oxygen sensor, the one the catalyst check reads; the front A/F sensor threads into the turbo outlet and does not move. So a downpipe flange leak shows on the rear sensor and the catalyst code, not on fuel trims. Most 200-cell pipes set P0420 within days; owners of 400-cell pipes report none. An oxygen sensor spacer is hit-and-miss: it can swap P0420 for a slow-response P1039. In KTuner the switch lives under Main Parameters, then Disables and Monitors, at the P0420 catalyst efficiency entry, and this car keeps it on. The đăng kiểm inspection tests tailpipe gas and checks that the warning lamp works; switching the code off hides a fault and does nothing for the gas test. Prefer a 400-cell catted pipe, check both flanges for leaks with the engine cold, and keep the monitor on.

nodes.label: kc-power-sources
nodes.description: More air, more fire, more fuel? Where power comes from
nodes.topics: power, torque, boost, fuel, ignition, air
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks how to make more power or torque, or asks for more fuel, more timing or more boost.
nodes.body: Only air makes power. Torque follows the mass of air trapped in each cylinder, and boost is a pressure, not a flow. Fuel follows air: best power sits near lambda 0.82 to 0.85, and this map asks 0.75 on purpose to cool the charge against knock and keep turbine heat down, so more fuel adds nothing and leaner is wrong on hot E10 RON95. Spark is capped by knock before its best point on pump fuel, so more boost on this fuel forces timing out: about the same power, more heat. Honda's ECU is torque-based: the pedal asks for torque, the ECU sets boost and throttle, and its factory torque limiter caps the result to protect the CVT. A downpipe makes the same air cheaper to get; it does not lift that cap.

nodes.label: kc-prl-hvi-factory
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED The PRL HVI keeps the factory curve
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Not verified. The vendor promises proper trims with no tune and calibrators treat the street housing as its own option, but nobody published its diameter against factory. Never infer the curve from the brand: ask which housing is fitted, then set the matching option. See the current card.

nodes.label: kc-quick-adjustments
nodes.description: Throttle response and turbo lag live in Quick Adjustments
nodes.topics: response, lag, throttle, spool, ktuner, quick-adjustments
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks for sharper throttle response, less turbo lag, or about Early Spool.
nodes.body: Response and lag live in KTuner's Quick Adjustments dropdowns, not in map tables, and on this car every level is Factory: Throttle Responsiveness, Boost Target Ramp Rate and each tune's Turbo Responsiveness. Throttle Responsiveness is pedal feel, not power, and no log can prove it, so it is your taste. For lag, a floored pull shows the cause: time from the pedal at 85 percent to boost at 90 percent of target, read with the wastegate. If the target ramps slowly while the wastegate is still open, one level up on Turbo Responsiveness or Boost Target Ramp Rate can help, one change at a time, proven on matched pulls. If the wastegate is shut and boost still lags, that is the turbo itself and no setting helps. Early Spool stays off: it adds low-rpm torque where the CVT and pre-ignition risk sit. The app explains these; it never writes them.

nodes.label: kc-ranges
nodes.description: Knock Control ranges and what each level costs
nodes.applies_when: Any reply that names a Knock Control level or a timing cost.
nodes.body: The Fuel-quality score reads 0.49 at its best, and higher means timing is pulled everywhere. Watch starts at 0.56. No hard driving starts at 0.62 held over 60 seconds. Stop starts at 0.80, which this car has never reached. Under boost each point above the floor costs 10.2 degrees, so 0.56 costs about 0.7 degrees, 0.62 costs about 1.3 degrees, 0.65 costs about 1.6 degrees, and 0.80 would cost about 3.2 degrees. The 5.0 degrees of retard logged under boost at 0.49 is scheduled from the score, not knock events. Cool drives end at 0.49 to 0.53, and the hottest traffic drive stayed below the 0.66 maximum seen on this car. The cut points are judgement, labelled as such, not measured limits.

nodes.label: kc-rich-wot
nodes.description: My full-throttle mixture reads richer than the map asks
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks whether a rich full-throttle reading is a fault, or blames E10.
nodes.body: The map asks 11.0 at full load, which is 0.75 in lambda, and this car reads 10.1 to 10.7 there, or 0.69 to 0.73 against the 0.75 asked. Richer than asked is the safe side for knock and heat, not a fault, though it costs a little power: best power sits leaner, near 0.82 to 0.85. Every logged reading sits at 11.3 or richer. E10 does not make it lean: the sensor measures lambda whatever the fuel, and no fuel is added for E10. The mixture is judged at 12 psi and above, where the full-load target applies. Watch starts half an AFR leaner than asked, and danger starts at 12.0, a full AFR leaner. Without the live lambda command channel, lower-load cells with leaner targets stay out of the verdict.

nodes.label: kc-shakedown
nodes.description: The Shakedown drive after any Flash
nodes.applies_when: A Flash was just recorded, or the Next step asks for a calm proving drive.
nodes.body: After any Flash, drive calm for 10 minutes before any hard acceleration: steady speeds, no pulls, engine fully warm. Watch the trims first and the score second. Hard driving waits until a calm stretch shows trims within 5 percent; that is what proves the new map measures air correctly. Save the earlier file under its own name before flashing, so Undo is one flash back. If the trims never settle, or a new Stop appears on the Shakedown itself, flash back and say so: the Flash is not credited until a drive proves it.

nodes.label: kc-stock-sensor-accurate
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED The stock sensor is accurate enough under boost
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Removed. Nothing read supports or rejects it, so no verdict rests on absolute sensor accuracy. The mixture is judged against the map's own target, where a small fixed offset matters less, and a wideband check stays the gold standard. See the current card.

nodes.label: kc-table-boost
nodes.description: The boost tables in KTuner
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks what a boost table does, wants more boost, or a boost change is in the plan.
nodes.body: Each of the three tunes has its own Boost Target tables, Normal and ECO, each Low and High cam: rpm by load tables of the boost the ECU aims for. On this map Normal plateaus at 21 psi from 4,000 rpm, ECO keeps factory-like boost, and as digitized the three tunes hold the same values. Final Boost Target is the target after the ECU arbitrates, topping out near 23.4. Boost By Gear Limits is flat, so no gear limit is active. The logged target has never passed 19.2 psi: the factory throttle dampening and the Boost Target Ramp Rate hold it, so it follows the pedal and climbs over seconds. Cylinder Fill Limitation is a knock safeguard; the everyday cap is the factory torque limiter, which KTuner does not expose. Low-rpm torque is what hurts the CVT, so good maps keep boost down there. Change the paired tables together.

nodes.label: kc-table-ignition
nodes.description: Ignition tables: read them, don't add timing on the street
nodes.topics: ignition, timing, spark, knock, tables, ktuner
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks about ignition, timing or knock-sensitivity tables, or asks for more timing.
nodes.body: Ignition Base (Low and High cam) is the main spark map by rpm and load; Ignition Max is a ceiling; Ethanol Ign Adj adds timing for ethanol; the Knock Sens tables set how sensitive knock detection is. KTuner's own formula: final timing is the ignition table plus the knock limit, minus the timing Knock Control pulls. Best timing can't be seen from a street log, so the street rule is: start from a professional basemap, log Knock Control trends over several pulls, and only ever remove timing, in steps of 1 to 2 degrees, where retard collects. Never add timing or lower knock sensitivity without a dyno. This app reads these tables but doesn't edit them.

nodes.label: kc-table-maf
nodes.description: The airflow (MAF Scaling) table comes first
nodes.topics: maf, afm, airflow, trims, tables, ktuner, intake
nodes.applies_when: Trims are off, an intake was fitted, or the owner asks what MAF Scaling does.
nodes.body: MAF Scaling turns the airflow sensor's frequency into grams of air, over 103 points. Every fuel calculation starts from it, which is why tuners fix airflow before anything else. Presets exist per intake housing: Factory, and Race presets for the larger housings; Custom is the one you edit. A tuner corrects it from steady part-throttle trims, bin by bin, applying only part of the correction each round and keeping the curve smooth, then flashes and logs again until trims sit within about 5 percent. Up to about 10 percent is commonly called normal; beyond that the table, or the preset, is wrong.

nodes.label: kc-table-wot
nodes.description: WOT Enrichment is the full-throttle mixture target
nodes.topics: afr, mixture, lambda, wot, tables, ktuner
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks about AFR, lambda or WOT Enrichment, or a mixture change is in the plan.
nodes.body: WOT Enrichment (WOT Enrich in the map file; its load axis is the air per stroke, in milligrams) holds the mixture the ECU aims for, by rpm and load, Low and High cam. KTuner's Nominal Lambda for Component Protection page is for the Type R, not this car. Cruise and light load stay at 14.7 for the catalyst; the highest load columns ask 11.0. It is a target, not a fix: change it only after the airflow table is right, with trims within 5 percent, and in steps of 0.2 AFR or less, watching Knock Control on every pull. Leaner at full throttle trades knock and exhaust heat margin for a little power; richer than asked is safe. Low and High are changed together.

nodes.label: kc-timing-percent
nodes.description: Should I add 2 or 5 percent timing?
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks to add timing by a percentage, or to try more timing and see what happens.
nodes.body: No. Honda's ECU never runs more timing than Ignition Base; it only takes timing away through Knock Control, and on E10 RON95 this car already sits at the 0.49 floor under boost, so the table is the timing. A percent works the wrong way here: Ignition Base holds 150 negative cells, the high-load ones where boost lives, and plus 5 percent makes them more negative, about 0.08 degrees less on a typical boosted cell, while it adds about 1 degree in cruise cells that are already near ideal. Every tuner works in degrees and adds timing only on a dyno, keeping 2 to 3 degrees from knock. On the street the sound move is the reverse: remove timing in degrees where Knock Control rises repeatably. That stays teach-only here until a load channel is logged.

nodes.label: kc-torque-250nm
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED Keep CVT torque under 250 Nm
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Removed. A warning seen only in excerpts, with the unit disputed, while the vendor's own page adds more than that over stock. No torque number is used for this car; judge fluid heat and slip instead. See the current card.

nodes.label: kc-trim-cause
nodes.description: The trim pattern names one cause
nodes.applies_when: Trims are off and the owner changed something, or a Stop names trims.
nodes.body: Trims beyond 10 percent in every load band, from the first minute, right after a Flash or a fitted part, usually mean the airflow preset does not match the intake housing. Trims 15 percent or worse everywhere after a change mean Undo first: flash back the earlier file, then pick the preset for the housing. Trims wrong only at idle and low airflow, fine higher up, usually mean unmetered air, a leak after the sensor: check clamps and flanges with the engine cold, no map change. Never bend the airflow curve to cancel a preset mismatch, and never touch full-throttle targets for a trim fault. Prove it with a calm drive and trims within 5 percent.

nodes.label: kc-trims
nodes.description: Trims within 5 percent are fine, beyond 10 is a Stop
nodes.applies_when: Any reply that judges fuel trims or air measurement.
nodes.body: Trims within 5 percent either way are fine, and beyond 10 percent either way is a Stop. On this car warm cruise trims sit at a median of 0.8 percent negative, with the middle band from 3.1 percent negative to 1.6 percent positive, all on E10, so there is no E10 offset to subtract. The one fault drive sat at 28 percent negative median total trim, far outside anything healthy. A Stop here means the ECU cannot measure air correctly, so hard driving waits until a calm drive shows trims back within 5 percent. The cause comes from the trim pattern, never from the size of the number alone.

nodes.label: kc-tune-one-thing
nodes.description: How a careful tuner changes a map from logs
nodes.topics: tune, method, log, fuel, ignition, flash, rules
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks how tuning from logs works, or wants to change several things at once.
nodes.body: Read the whole log before touching anything, and remember which cells you already changed so no cell is corrected twice from the same evidence. Change one thing per round: fuel or airflow first, log again, and only then look at spark. Apply only part of what the log suggests, then let the next log show the rest. Judge with the engine fully warm, from mid-gear pulls, never first gear, and roll into the throttle instead of stabbing it. Never add timing on the street. After hard logging, let a turbo engine idle a minute before switching off. A Knock Count blip alone can be noise; repeated evidence decides.

nodes.label: kc-tune-order
nodes.description: The order a tuner works in
nodes.topics: tuning, order, safety, airflow, fuel, ignition, boost
nodes.applies_when: Before any map change, and when the owner asks why one table comes before another.
nodes.body: Every log is read in the same order. First, is the log usable. Second, safety: anything lean under boost, a step up in Knock Control, fuel pressure under target, or heat — stop and find the cause. Third, air before fuel: trims against airflow show whether the airflow table matches the intake; never fix a scaling error with fuel targets. Fourth, fuel against its target under boost. Spark is the ECU's job: rising Knock Control means less margin, and the remedy is fuel, heat or boost, not more timing on the street. Then boost, actual against target. One change, one reflash, one log under the same conditions.

nodes.label: kc-wot-lean-display
nodes.description: SUPERSEDED Real lambda reads leaner than shown on E10
nodes.applies_when: Never returned as current. Kept so the agent never repeats it.
nodes.body: Refuted. The sensor measures lambda whatever the fuel, and the log shows lambda times the gasoline scale, so what is shown is the real lambda. This car runs richer than asked under boost on E10. See the current card.

nodes.label: kc-wot-lean-timing
nodes.description: Leaning the full-throttle mixture can cost timing, not add power
nodes.topics: mixture, wot, afr, ignition, timing, power, e10
nodes.applies_when: The owner asks to lean the full-throttle target for power, or why the mixture lever is locked.
nodes.body: An owner who calibrated his own 1.5T found that running full-throttle mixture near or past 11.5 made the ECU pull timing hard, so it lost power instead of gaining it; 11 to 11.2 worked best on his car. That is one car, not a rule, but it is the same direction this car's data points: no gain shown from leaning, and a real risk. That is why the shop keeps the full-throttle mixture target where the basemap has it. What would change that is a log with AFR Command, the car healthy in heat, and a like-for-like proof drive.

nodes.label: The CVT survives 300 whp
nodes.description: Community figure: about 250-260 lb-ft at the wheels. PRL's 300 whp car made 304 lb-ft on a manual; buyers asked them to test a CVT and no result is published.

nodes.label: A catted downpipe adds about 12 whp with no tune
nodes.description: 27WON vendor dyno on the factory ECU: +12 whp / +13 lb-ft peak; their first CVT test gave +7 / +11. No independent 11th-gen dyno. 27WON says a CEL can be illuminated (owners report it within days); TSP says theirs will not.

nodes.label: Hondata basemap: +34 hp / +50 lb-ft
nodes.description: Vendor claim, on Hondata's own chart: 22 Civic 1.5, 91 octane. The chart does not show the transmission.

nodes.label: KTuner basemaps: Starter 16.5, 18 and 21 psi
nodes.description: Starter 18 (Stage 1): up to +30 whp. Starter 21 (Stage 2): up to +55 whp. "Running 91+ will give the best results." Your file is Starter 21 Dual Tune 2.

nodes.label: Stock MAP sensors stop reading at about 26-28 psi
nodes.description: Two vendors agree. 4-bar sensors read to about 45 psi and must be enabled in KTuner (supported on the 22+ non-Si).

nodes.label: A drop-in turbo makes 300 whp on this engine
nodes.description: PRL 308 whp and RV6 281 whp on 93 octane; 335-341 whp on E26-E30. All shown on manual cars. 27WON: "With 91 octane, sometimes you just can't reach 300WHP."

nodes.label: Phearable Stage 1.5 runs about 16.4 / 18 / 23-24 psi
nodes.description: 194 hp / 237 lb-ft on a stock 2022 non-Si CVT. 93 recommended, 91 the absolute minimum.

nodes.label: Vietnam E10 RON95 is "premium" like US 91/93
nodes.description: E10RON95 is still RON 95. US pumps show (RON+MON)/2, so RON 95 is about US 91: the floor of those maps, not 93.

nodes.label: Thai FE: stock turbo + intercooler + downpipe + E20 remap = 237 hp / 350 Nm
nodes.description: One shop clip, no dyno sheet. E20 is not sold in Vietnam.

nodes.label: TSP Stage 1 for the non-Si CVT has a 24 psi map
nodes.description: Map 3: 24 psi in Normal/Sport, 16.5 psi in ECO. Map 2: 16.5 psi. Premium 91/93 required, no E85.

nodes.label: The stock turbo can run the 21-24 psi maps
nodes.description: In your hard-pull drive the wastegate is about 3 % open at the boost peak, measured at ≤ 19.9 psi: the stock turbo is near its limit before your 21 psi target.

Air before fuel
nodes.description: Trims against airflow show whether the airflow table matches the intake. Wrong everywhere right after a part or a Flash points to the preset for the housing; never fix a scaling error with fuel targets.

nodes.label: Boost last, one proven step
nodes.description: Boost comes last because every earlier stage must hold under it. A raise is one small step on the second tune only, offered only after floored pulls on a Cool drive and a hot drive pass every gate, so switching tunes undoes it.

nodes.label: Flash and confirm
nodes.description: The owner types the cells into KTuner, flashes, and confirms. The next log is read back against the plan, so a typo or a missed table shows up before it is judged.

nodes.label: Take the car in
nodes.description: A shop writes the car down before it touches the map: parts fitted, intake housing, fuel, basemap, what the owner wants. It sets expectations first: on this basemap the turbo has little headroom left, so the early rounds buy safety and consistency, not power.

nodes.label: Keep it, then the next round
nodes.description: A proven change becomes the new Map version and the Baseline moves with it. The round ends; the next one starts from a fresh log. Rounds stop when the logs ask nothing more of the map.

nodes.label: Log a Drive the shop can read
nodes.description: Every round starts with a log taken the way the shop asks: every gauge the shop reads turned on, the fastest rate, a warm engine, pulls on a cool morning when boost is the question. A log that skips this costs a round.

nodes.label: Fuel against its target under boost
nodes.description: Full-throttle mixture is judged against the map's own target, cell by cell. Richer than asked is the safe side on E10 in the heat; leaning it for power can cost timing instead.

nodes.label: One change: the Flash plan
nodes.description: One family per Flash, the earliest in tune order that needs it. The engine writes the cells; two independent checks pass them before the owner sees them. "No map change" is a plan too.

nodes.label: Prove it, like for like
nodes.description: A calm Shakedown drive first, then the drive the change needs, under the same conditions as the one before it. Weather and fuel move between logs; comparing unlike drives is how e-tunes lose weeks.

nodes.label: Is the log usable?
nodes.description: Gate zero. A short drive, a slow rate or a stuck gauge settles nothing, so the shop says what to fix in the logger and asks for the drive again instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Safety first
nodes.description: Before any change: anything lean under boost, a step up in Knock Control, fuel pressure under target, or heat. Ranked by what it protects: the engine first, then the CVT, then power. A Stop ends the round here.

nodes.label: Spark is the ECU's job
nodes.description: Ignition and knock sensitivity are read, never edited on the street. Rising Knock Control means less margin; the remedy is fuel, heat or boost, not more timing.

nodes.label: Undo first
nodes.description: When a Stop follows a Flash, the cheapest proven fix is the file that ran before it. Flash it back, then find the cause.

nodes.label: Baseline
nodes.description: This car's own normal value for a measure, judged from its cool drives; limits are set as distance from the baseline, not from forum numbers.

nodes.label: Boost step
nodes.description: A Flash plan that raises the Normal boost targets by 1 psi at 3,000 rpm and above, offered only after the logs pass every safety gate and kept only when the next Cool drive and a hot drive prove the turbo reaches the new target without knock or lean; the first failed gate undoes it.

nodes.label: Capabilities
nodes.description: What the assistant can do, can do with a limit, and can't do, kept as one list the agents, the cards and the owner all read.

nodes.label: Car file
nodes.description: Everything the shop keeps about the one car: the Car profile, its Installs, Map versions and Flashes, the Logger setup, the Car history and where the car is in its Round. Every chat reads it; no chat owns it.

nodes.label: Car history
nodes.description: The remembered summary of every drive the owner has checked, in time order, used to see this car change over time.

nodes.label: Car profile
nodes.description: The owner's one car as the app knows it: model, transmission, fuel, climate, the parts fitted, and the KTuner basemap it started from.

nodes.label: Chat
nodes.description: One conversation with the shop, kept and listed; its title comes from its first message. Deleting a chat never deletes a Drive, a Flash or a Map version.

nodes.label: Cool drive
nodes.description: A drive with intake air under 42 °C while moving; the only kind that can set the Baseline.

nodes.label: Drive
nodes.description: One TunerView log of one trip, identified by its start time.

nodes.label: Drive brief
nodes.description: The drive the shop asks for, written as a customer brief: where and when, warm-up, the cruise for trims, the pulls (gear mode, from what speed, how far, the break between), how long, which gauges and how fast to log, and the checkpoints the log will be read against.

nodes.label: Drives to proof
nodes.description: The number of Drives from the moment a Next step is given to the Drive that settles it; fewer is the product's win.

nodes.label: Flash
nodes.description: A change of map written to the ECU, recorded by the owner with a date, the map name and what changed (AFM preset, boost, fuel, other).

nodes.label: Flash plan
nodes.description: The single set of map changes proposed for the next Flash: one table family, with evidence, proof and undo; it can also be "Undo" or "no change".

nodes.label: Flash readback
nodes.description: The check, on the first Drive after a Flash, that what the ECU runs matches the Map version that was planned (logged boost targets against the changed cells, trims against the MAF Scaling choice); a mismatch means the Flash is not credited.

nodes.label: Front agent
nodes.description: The model that reads every typed message first and decides with tools: show where the car is, open the car editor, show the drive brief, say what the shop can and can't do, or hand the question to the tuner. A greeting is never answered with a knowledge card.

nodes.label: Fuel tag
nodes.description: The fuel in the tank when a log was recorded (E10 RON95 III or E10 RON97 III), chosen by the owner when attaching the log.

nodes.label: Fuel-quality score (Knock Control)
nodes.description: The ECU's learned knock margin for the current fuel and heat; 0.49 is the best it can read, and higher means timing is pulled everywhere.

nodes.label: Goal
nodes.description: What the owner wants from the car: daily, spirited or economy. It reorders options and wording, never unlocks a change.

nodes.label: Health report
nodes.description: The engine's checks of a Drive grouped by system (Fuel, Air & boost, Spark, Heat, CVT), each with its value and Verdict word.

nodes.label: Hidden drive
nodes.description: A drive the owner has left out of the Car history (lent car, idle test, logger fault); its log is untouched and it never sets the Baseline.

nodes.label: History file
nodes.description: One file the owner exports and imports holding the Car history and every Flash; the only copy of Flash records outside the browser.

nodes.label: Hot restart
nodes.description: A drive started within 30 minutes of the previous one with the intake already at 50 °C or more.

nodes.label: Install
nodes.description: A part fitted to or removed from the car, recorded with its date; like a Flash, it explains a change in the drives that follow.

nodes.label: KTuner basemap
nodes.description: One of KTuner's shipped starting maps (this car: Starter 21 Dual Tune 2); reverting to it makes it the active Map version.

nodes.label: Key moment
nodes.description: A point in a drive worth the owner's attention (a Stop starting, a score step, a hard pull, lugging, a hot restart), shown with its clock time.

nodes.label: Knowledge proposal
nodes.description: A fact the assistant needed but no knowledge card holds; recorded for review in `knowledge/proposed/` instead of being stated, and never cited until a reviewer sources it into a card.

nodes.label: Log checkpoints
nodes.description: After an upload, whether the log met the Drive brief, one line each: logging rate, moving time, every gauge moving, AFR Command and MAF Hz logged, engine warm, cool intake, two pulls, pull-start intake. Met, not met, or can't say.

nodes.label: Logger setup
nodes.description: What the owner's TunerView logged last time: the gauges seen, the logging rate, and what was missing (AFR Command, MAF Hz); the Drive brief opens with what to fix.

nodes.label: Map
nodes.description: The calibration file on the ECU. A drive's map is the Map version active when it started; it is never guessed from the log.

nodes.label: Map slot
nodes.description: Which of the maps KTuner can switch between on the fly a Drive ran on, chosen by the owner when attaching the log. Drives on different slots are never compared.

nodes.label: Map tour
nodes.description: The whole map at a high level, family by family in the order a tuner works (airflow, full-throttle mixture, boost, ignition, knock sensitivity, left to the basemap), each with its status this Round: this round, locked (why, and what unlocks it), no change needed, or read-only.

nodes.label: Map version
nodes.description: One numbered copy of the Map's tables kept by the app: the first is the map the owner gave the app, and each Flash plan the owner confirms flashing becomes the next one.

nodes.label: Next step
nodes.description: The one thing the app asks of the owner after each Drive: a Flash (from the Flash plan), a gauge to watch, a drive to log, or nothing; it always names the drive whose upload will settle it.

nodes.label: Open step
nodes.description: A Next step still waiting for the Drive that proves or disproves it.

nodes.label: Premium-fuel test
nodes.description: The comparison of two fuels on matched Drives (both with hard pulls, intake within 8 °C, same Map slot) by the Fuel-quality score and the timing it costs; a gap of 0.5° or less is inside KTuner's logging step, so no measurable difference.

nodes.label: Read-only table
nodes.description: A table the assistant reads and explains but never proposes a value for (ignition, knock sensitivity, and the tables left to the basemap).

nodes.label: Recap
nodes.description: The first reply of a new Chat for a known car: the car in one line, Round N on its Map version, the last Drive and its Verdict, the Next step and what it waits for.

nodes.label: Round
nodes.description: One turn of the shop's loop: log the brief, read it, change and flash, prove it with the next log. Rounds are counted from Flashes (Round N = Flashes so far + 1), not from the Map version number, because an Undo returns to an earlier version.

nodes.label: Safety channel
nodes.description: One of the four channels a safe verdict cannot do without: mixture, fuel trims, Fuel-quality score, fuel pressure. If one is flat or missing, the drive's verdict is Can't tell.

nodes.label: Shakedown drive
nodes.description: The first drive after a Flash, during which hard driving waits until a calm stretch shows the new map is measuring air and fuel correctly.

nodes.label: Suggested replies
nodes.description: Up to three chips under the latest reply, written by the model from the reply and the stage and checked by the app; else the stage's own.

nodes.label: Timing pulled
nodes.description: The degrees of ignition timing the ECU removes because of the Fuel-quality score, shown against this car's normal.

nodes.label: Too-short drive
nodes.description: A drive with under 60 s of moving; it gets no verdict and stays out of the Car history.

nodes.label: Unexplained change
nodes.description: A jump against the Car history (trims, boost target, or a high starting Fuel-quality score) with no Flash recorded to explain it.

nodes.label: Verdict
nodes.description: One of four words for a safety line or a whole drive: **OK**, **Watch**, **Stop**, **Can't tell**. **Stop** means danger to the engine or CVT now, never a broken procedure. "No hard driving" is a Watch with that sentence, not a fifth word.

nodes.label: Wasted drive
nodes.description: A Drive that could settle none of the Open steps: too short, the wrong conditions (hot when the step needs cool), or a logger fault.

nodes.label: boost_ceiling_psi
nodes.description: A rule, not a fixed number: no boost cell above the active map's Final Boost Target peak at that cell's rpm row (the lower of the two rows either side), and never above 24 psi. Each +1 psi is proven by datalog (boost_step_gates).
nodes.source: ticket 06 D1 (the app writes up to the active map's Final Boost Target peak, 23.4 on Starter 21) and ticket 13 (24 psi: the highest any vendor file has run on this car); ADR 0007

nodes.label: boost_pairs
nodes.description: A boost change touches, with identical cells, either all six tables (safety trims), Tune 2 L and H alone (a Boost step) or Tunes 1 and 3 L and H (promote). A raise in Tune 1 or 3 is accepted only as a promote: each cell's after equals the current Tune 2 cell.
nodes.source: engine P6 (engine/kta-car.js carFlashPlan: the six Normal boost tables move together, verified in the file); ticket 16 (a Boost step is written to Tune 2 only, a proven step is copied to Tunes 1 and 3; safety trims write all three tunes)

nodes.label: boost_raise_min_rpm
nodes.description: Below 3,000 rpm boost may only be lowered, never raised.
nodes.source: fact-check.md §5 (LSPI band 1,500–2,500 rpm at high load) and §2 (the map carries ~11° retard at 1,500 rpm / −1 psi: the lugging zone is knock-prone)

nodes.label: boost_step_gates
nodes.description: A Boost step is offered, and kept, only when every gate passes on the latest Cool drive's proof pulls and the latest hot drive's Knock Control. No Honda tuner publishes these numbers: they are our judgement on the shared tuner method (ticket 13).
nodes.unit: mixed (%, s, rpm, psi, score, AFR, deg)
nodes.source: ticket 16 (proof pull: pedal 85 % held 4 s above 3,500 rpm, 2 pulls, rows 3,500-4,500; the pass gates), ticket 13 (overshoot tightened to 1.5 and target + overshoot 24; ignition achieved vs the last proven Map version, drop over 1°; DIFP 90 %; Knock Control 0.56 kept, read settled), ticket 17 (the logged target must reach the table: within 0.5 psi), ticket 06 D1 (undershoot 1.5, AFR never leaner than 12.0, trims ±5 %), ktuner-community-knowledge.md §6.5 (overshoot judged held 0.5 s: KTuner calls a 1-3 psi spike normal)

nodes.label: boost_step_max
nodes.description: No single cell moves more than 1 psi in one Flash.
nodes.source: fact-check.md §4 (wastegate 2.5 % median at 15 psi and up: the turbo is near its limit, so boost moves in small steps)

nodes.label: editable_tables
nodes.description: The only tables a Flash may touch, each with its one family.
nodes.source: engine KTA.TABLES (only role=edit tables ship in a Flash; test/thresholds.test.js asserts the two lists match)

nodes.label: forbidden_tables
nodes.description: Ignition, knock-sensitivity and protection tables never appear in a change; neither does any other table the basic stage leaves alone.
nodes.source: fact-check.md §2 (timing = table + limitation − retard; the remedy is never desensitize the knock sensors) and engine KTA.TABLES roles leave/never/check/preset/info

nodes.label: maf_curve_rising
nodes.description: After the change the MAF Scaling curve must still rise at every point.
nodes.source: data/ktuner-maps-digitized.json (all four MAF Scaling curves rise at every point; test/engine.test.js asserts it)

nodes.label: maf_step_max_pct
nodes.description: No MAF Scaling point moves more than ±10 % per round.
nodes.source: fact-check.md §6 (cruise trims within ±5 % are OK, beyond ±10 % is a Stop: one round stays inside the healthy band)

nodes.label: one_family_per_flash
nodes.description: Every table in a change belongs to one family: AFM Flow, boost or mixture.
nodes.source: engine P4 (engine/kta-car.js carFlashPlan: one table family per Flash, the rest wait to be proven)

nodes.label: wot_pairs
nodes.description: A mixture change touches both WOT tables with identical cells, or neither.
nodes.source: engine P6 (engine/kta-car.js carFlashPlan: WOT L=H, verified in the file)

nodes.label: wot_target_band
nodes.description: WOT targets stay inside 11.0–12.0 AFR on the gasoline scale.
nodes.source: fact-check.md §6 (the map file: WOT_Enrich top load columns ask 11.0, λ 0.75, at full load)

nodes.label: The CVT
nodes.description: CVT care is heat management; the ECU's own torque limiter protects it. Fluid temperature and slip are read every drive; hard pulls wait for a cool gearbox.

nodes.label: Vietnam E10 RON95
nodes.description: E10 needs no extra fuel and no trim offset. Octane sets the knock margin, so fuel is tested tank against tank by Knock Control, never by feel.

nodes.label: Heat soak and hot intake air
nodes.description: Hot traffic and restarts soak the intake; timing comes out on a schedule before any knock. Judge power and boost on Cool drives, and treat a hot drive as the stress test.

nodes.label: The logger and its gauges
nodes.description: The shop can only judge what was logged. Missing channels make gates read Can't tell; a flat channel wastes the drive.

nodes.label: Lugging and oil
nodes.description: Low revs under real load are what raise Knock Control in traffic. A habit to change and an oil grade to keep, not a map change.
